david: quick heads-up — after yesterday's runtime rollout i'm seeing memory spikes and a handful of OOMs on our paged-attention model shards. seems correlated with higher concurrency and long KV cache lifetimes. anyone else see this?

nina: which model + commit? can you repro locally or share a profile? :thinking:

david: repros on prod-ish canary (commit f3a9b2c). model: redwood/opt-2.7b, seq_len 2048, steady qps ~1200. KV cache growth looks normal but block manager does frequent compaction sweeps and we get spikes of cudaMallocs right before OOM. attaching small excerpt of logs: 

```
W blockmgr: compacting 24 blocks -> moved 18, freed 6, compaction_cost_ms=42
I kvcache: reserve_block(0x7f8c) -> size=256k
E allocator: cudaMalloc failed after 3.1s, retrying
OOM on device 0, requested 1.2GB
```

omar: i pulled a flamegraph from the perf pod — allocation hot paths are very noisy. big tail on cudaMalloc and free storms from compaction. looks like fragmentation + many small allocations. my notes: "arena size too small -> lots of dmallocs".

jia: two quick levers to try: 1) allocator tuning (increase default arena / enable cudaMallocAsync pool) 2) workspace sizing + reservation for hot KV slots so we avoid repeated alloc/free during compaction. also consider buffer reuse for temporary attention blocks.

omar: yep. i ran a small experiment locally: switched allocator to pooled async path and bumped per-gpu arena from 64MB -> 256MB. result: peak cudaMalloc count dropped ~85%, latency tail improved. snippet: 

```
config: {
  allocator: cuda_async_pool,
  arena_size: 268435456, // 256MB
  enable_workspace_reserve: true
}
benchmark: {
  baseline_peak_allocs: 1420,
  tuned_peak_allocs: 210,
  p99_infer_ms: 78 -> 61
}
```

omar: important caveat — enabling cudaMallocAsync changes lifetime semantics; must ensure we return buffers to pool promptly or we bloat the pool. also watch fragmentation if block sizes mismatch.

david: on the paged-attn side, our block manager default block_size is 256kb. we've been testing 512kb as an option. tradeoffs: larger blocks reduce header overhead and compactions, but increase wasted memory on partially filled blocks. thoughts?

nina: smaller block_size -> more compaction activity (higher CPU + free/alloc churn). larger block_size -> higher internal slack but fewer allocations -> less fragmentation. for our workload (KV entries ~40–200B), 256kb seems to produce many partially filled blocks. 512kb might be sweet spot. also think about block reuse policy (MRU vs FIFO) and compaction threshold.

omar: i ran a quick matrix combining block_size and allocator pool: 

```
results:
- block=256k + default alloc: p99=120ms, mem_peak=18.1GB, alloc_calls=1780
- block=256k + async pool: p99=90ms, mem_peak=15.9GB, alloc_calls=320
- block=512k + async pool: p99=68ms, mem_peak=16.8GB, alloc_calls=210
- block=1MB   + async pool: p99=72ms, mem_peak=18.9GB, alloc_calls=140
```

omar: conclusion: 512k + async pool gives best tail latency with moderate memory footprint. 1MB reduces alloc calls further but wastes memory.

jia: for immediate mitigation i'd: 
- enable cudaMallocAsync pool on canary nodes
- increase arena to 256MB
- bump paged-attn block_size default to 512k behind a rollout flag
- add a soft reservation for the most-used KV slots so they land in the pool early
- add metrics for alloc_call_count, pool_high_water, compaction_runs

perf-bot: CI perf-run f3a9b2c -> canary build shows regression: p99 +12% vs baseline on master. see /ci/perf/174800 for details. :robot_face:

david: i'll open a small PR with config flags + one-line default bump for block_size and allocator mode. will run canary with subset of capacity. can someone review quickly? @nina @omar?

nina: happy to review — will prioritize this afternoon. also please include a reproducible perf-test harness snippet so I can run locally.

omar: i'll help with metrics + perf script. i'll also add a guard to ensure compaction doesn't try to reallocate >75% of GPU memory in a single sweep (to avoid cascading OOMs).

ops-bot: scheduled canary deployment: cluster=prod-us-east-1, nodes=5 (canary), start=1748001300 UTC. :gear:


david: thanks all. next steps: patch -> canary -> observe alloc_call_count/pool_high_water/compaction_runs for 24h. if stable, gradual rollout. will file follow-ups for: better block reuse heuristics and async compaction strategy. :thumbsup:

nina: nits: add docs on memory semantics when cudaMallocAsync is enabled and a note in release notes about block_size change.

david: noted. i'll include that in PR description.
__notes: This thread contains a short technical Slack discussion about paged attention memory issues, allocator tuning, block size tradeoffs, profiling snippets, and a small rollout plan. Messages are intentionally short and choppy to mimic Slack style.
